descriptionTemplate.label: Data Management Plan Template - University of Bologna
descriptionTemplate.description:
This template has been prepared by the Data Stewards of the University of Bologna to support researchers in drafting a Data Management Plan for their project. It consists of a form designed to describe any research output (data, software and/or non-digital objects) in turn and how it is managed throughout the project.

  • Section 1 asks about the research output creator(s) and allows to select which research output (data, software and/or non-digital objects) is being described. 
  • Section 2 is devoted to a description of the research output -- the questions here change according to the type of output selected in Section 1.
  • Section 3 asks you to describe the legal and ethical implications (if any) of handling the research output.
  • Section 4 asks you to describe how the research output is made Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable (FAIR).
  • Section 5 asks you to describe how data quality and integrity are ensured throughout the project.

The dataset contains several folders, one for each university involved. Each folder contains the following sub-directories:
  • iris_in_oc_meta contains basic bibliographic information of the IRIS publication recognised in OpenCitations Meta;
  • iris_in_oc_index contains all the citations extracted from OpenCitations Index that involve any of the IRIS publications included in iris_in_oc_meta;
  • iris_no_pid contains basic bibliographic information of the IRIS publications that do not specify any of the PIDs (i.e. DOI, PMID, ISBN) necessary for mapping them with the entries in OpenCitations Meta;
  • iris_not_in_meta contains basic bibliographic information for IRIS publications with the requested PIDs that were not recognised in OpenCitations Meta.
In addition, the archive contains two additional files:
  • logs, which contains the printed logs of the process executed to obtain the aforementioned data;
  • Mapping_IRIS_MIUR.xlsx, which maps the IRIS publication types with the national categories defined by the Italian Ministry of University and Research.
The dataset can be accessed on Zenodo at the following link: https://zenodo.org/records/18202530
These are the data produced for the analysis described in the article "Assessing and Comparing the Coverage of Publications of Italian Universities in Open Infrastructures".

This dataset is a derivative collection of bibliographic metadata retrieved from the OpenCitations Meta dataset. It contains specific information for citing and cited entities not previously included in the source dataset. The new data is structured to enable the mapping of institutional and geographic citation patterns to address the “Map of Italian Science” research question.
During the project, the material will be stored in a specific folder on the GitHub repository, while the research output will be published on Zenodo.

Data collection via the OpenCitations Meta API is necessary to fill a critical gap in the existing source dataset, which primarily contains records for the IRIS publications themselves. To answer the research question regarding the “Map of Italian Science”, we must retrieve missing metadata for the external entities that either cite or are cited by these publications.

Data has been collected using the REST API for OpenCitations Meta. The collection process will involve sending GET requests to a specific endpoint (https://api.opencitations.net/meta/v1/metadata/) using the parameter OMID.
All processed data will be preserved to ensure the study is fully reproducible. No data needs to be destroyed for legal reasons as all source data is open.
The entire process will be documented with README files, a notebook to keep track of the workflow, and a final paper.

description.description: To ensure a consistent analysis of disciplinary citation flows, we rely on a pre-existing SKOS alignment dataset that maps multiple classification systems to the Library of Congress scheme. This dataset is crucial because disciplinary information retrieved from sources such as DOAJ and SCIMAGO is expressed using heterogeneous and non-interoperable classification systems. Direct comparison would therefore be unreliable. The alignment dataset provides a curated and semantically grounded mapping between these systems, built through a systematic comparison of journal classifications across multiple databases. By using this resource, we avoid performing a new alignment from scratch and ensure a higher level of consistency and reliability in the mapping process.

This template has been prepared by the Data Stewards of the University of Bologna to support researchers in drafting a Data Management Plan for their project. It consists of a form designed to describe any research output (data, software and/or non-digital objects) in turn and how it is managed throughout the project.

  • Section 1 asks about the research output creator(s) and allows to select which research output (data, software and/or non-digital objects) is being described. 
  • Section 2 is devoted to a description of the research output -- the questions here change according to the type of output selected in Section 1.
  • Section 3 asks you to describe the legal and ethical implications (if any) of handling the research output.
  • Section 4 asks you to describe how the research output is made Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable (FAIR).
  • Section 5 asks you to describe how data quality and integrity are ensured throughout the project.

field.textValue: The methodology followed throughout the data lifecycle is described in this documentation published on GitHub: https://github.com/open-sci/2025-2026/blob/main/bloom/categories/Documantazione%20allineamento%20skos.pdf. The whole workflow can be also found here, in the README.md file: https://github.com/NicoleLiggeri/intership-OC.
Alma Mater Studiorum- Università di Bologna

The dataset is organised into three main components:
A. LoC + alignments (RDF/XML): a set of RDF files representing Library of Congress (LoC) classification concepts enriched with semantic alignments (e.g. skos:closeMatch, skos:narrowMatch) to categories from other classification systems.
B. Original categories (CSV): a collection of CSV files describing the hierarchical structure (broad and narrow categories) of the original classification systems (e.g. Scopus).
C. SKOS vocabularies of external systems (TTL): a set of SKOS vocabularies, expressed in Turtle format, modelling the classification systems of external sources as structured concept schemes, derived from the original CSV data.
The dataset can be found on GitHub: https://github.com/open-sci/2025-2026/tree/main/bloom/categories.

The dataset was created to identify and formalize correspondences between heterogeneous scientific classification systems across databases, enabling semantic alignment with the Library of Congress classification.
The data generation and alignment process is fully documented in: https://github.com/open-sci/2025-2026/blob/main/bloom/categories/Documantazione%20allineamento%20skos.pdf

The data we reuse are currently stored in a GitHub repository. Upon publication, we intend to deposit them in a permanent repository such as Zenodo, ensuring that they are accessible and citable as part of the resources used in this study, provided that the dataset owner agrees.

The resulting dataset, aligned with the Library of Congress classification, is encoded in RDF, while the source vocabularies are serialized in Turtle (TTL) format. The data are modeled using the SKOS (Simple Knowledge Organization System) standard.

The documentation is provided at this GitHub repository: https://github.com/open-sci/2025-2026/blob/main/bloom/categories/Documantazione%20allineamento%20skos.pdf. Other specifications about the project workflow are found here:https://github.com/NicoleLiggeri/intership-OC.

  • Generally, by 'vocabularies' or 'thesauri' we refer to those lexical resources composed of controlled terms to describe a set of elements, knowledge, data, theories belonging to a given scientific field or disciplinary domain.

ALMA MATER STUDIORIUM - University of Bologna

This dataset is a journal-level metadata collection provided by the Directory of Open Access Journals in CSV format. It contains structured information about open access academic journals worldwide.
The dataset includes 52 variables describing different aspects of each journal. These variables cover general information (such as journal title, ISSN, publisher, and country), access and licensing details (e.g., journal license, copyright policies, and open access compliance), editorial and review processes, publication fees (APC), and preservation services. It also includes metadata related to indexing and activity, such as subjects, keywords, number of article records, and dates of updates.
The data was collected to support the discovery, accessibility, and transparency of open access scholarly journals worldwide.

Data is collected through online applications submitted by journal publishers. DOAJ’s editorial team reviews and verifies this information before it is added to the database. Further information can be found here: https://doaj.org/apply/guide/

Not applicable as the preservation of this dataset will be handled directly by DOAJ. The copy we will use for our research will be preserved on our Github repository, as is, with no changes to the data.
DOAJ uses the LCC (Library of Congress Classification) for subject categorization. It also requires standard identifiers like ISSNs and DOIs.

The primary documentation is the CSV header row, which defines each of the 50+ metadata fields. Additionally, DOAJ provides a public API guide (https://doaj.org/api/v4/docs) and a blog, and a metadata FAQ page. (https://doaj.org/docs/faq/)

description.description: This dataset provides a ranked overview of the global institutions interacting with scholarly outputs from the six selected Italian IRIS instances (UNIBO, UNIMI, UNITO, UNIPD, UPO, SNS). It maps citation links retrieved from OpenCitations Index to the organizational metadata found in OpenCitations Meta, specifically focusing on the institutional affiliations of citing and cited authors. They aim of the dataset is identifying the most significant academic and research partners of the Italian university system and providing a ranking of countries based on the total volume of citations, offering an overview of the geographical distribution of the research impact.

descriptionTemplate.label: Data Management Plan Template - University of Bologna
descriptionTemplate.description:
This template has been prepared by the Data Stewards of the University of Bologna to support researchers in drafting a Data Management Plan for their project. It consists of a form designed to describe any research output (data, software and/or non-digital objects) in turn and how it is managed throughout the project.

  • Section 1 asks about the research output creator(s) and allows to select which research output (data, software and/or non-digital objects) is being described. 
  • Section 2 is devoted to a description of the research output -- the questions here change according to the type of output selected in Section 1.
  • Section 3 asks you to describe the legal and ethical implications (if any) of handling the research output.
  • Section 4 asks you to describe how the research output is made Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable (FAIR).
  • Section 5 asks you to describe how data quality and integrity are ensured throughout the project.

  • Generally, by 'vocabularies' or 'thesauri' we refer to those lexical resources composed of controlled terms to describe a set of elements, knowledge, data, theories belonging to a given scientific field or disciplinary domain.
  • With 'taxonomies', the elements are not only described by means of vocabularies of controlled and selected terms, but are also ordered in a system, generally hierarchical.
  • With 'ontologies', the types and thus the names of the relationships between the elements that make up a taxonomy or vocabulary are explicit. 
When collecting information, using at least a vocabulary can help can help to correctly identify the data and facilitate their reuse because they can be understood by others sharing a common vocabulary.

field.textValue: The dataset will be produced in open format and described by metadata standards.

The BLOOM IRIS-OC Inst-Geo Mapping dataset provides a ranked mapping of the global institutions and countries interacting with research from six Italian universities (UNIBO, UNIMI, UNITO, UNIPD, UPO, and SNS). It was generated by crossing bibliographic metadata from local IRIS instances with OpenCitations (Index and Meta), enriched with organizational data retrieved via the OpenCitations (https://opencitations.net), OpenAIRE (http://www.openaire.eu), and ROR (https://ror.org) APIs.
The dataset identifies and quantifies the specific entities that either cite or are cited by these universities through two primary outputs: a CSV file ranking individual institutions by citation frequency, and a second CSV file aggregating these results to rank countries by their total citation volume. Developed to analyze international scholarly influence, this resource highlights the most significant organizational and geographical research partners of the Italian academic system.
The research output will be published on Zenodo and available on the following repository: https://github.com/open-sci/2025-2026.

The data has been generated as part of a wider study on citation patterns among different italian institutions, aiming to map the institutional, geographical, and disciplinary citation networks of the six Italian universities taken in consideration. The results will be published in a paper.

The dataset is generated by cross-referencing bibliographic metadata from six Italian IRIS instances with the OpenCitations Index and Meta collections (Andreose, E., Heibi, I., Peroni, S., & Zilli, L. (2026). Data for the article "Assessing and Comparing the Coverage of Publications of Italian Universities in OpenCitations" (1.1.0) [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18202530). The process involves extracting citation links, identifying the institutional affiliations and the countries of the citing and cited entities and aggregating these occurrences into ranked frequency lists. Data provenance is maintained by documenting the specific OpenCitations snapshot used and version-controlling the Python-based transformation scripts via GitHub.
The entirety of the dataset can be preserved as it is.
The dataset will be documented by README files, a notebook file and the final paper.
